results.title: Nat'l football team veteran says having temporary coach not ideal
results.content: DOHA — Veteran midfielder Hwang In-beom claimed Monday having a caretaker boss is far from ideal for the national team, saying he would like more stability on the bench. Hwang and South Korea will play their sixth and likely final match under temporary head coach Robert Moreno on Tuesday against Qatar in Doha. Moreno was hired in early September, about two months after Hong Myung-bo resigned in light of South Korea's group-stage elimination at the FIFA World Cup. Korea Football Association (KFA) President Chung Mong-gyu also stepped down, creating a leadership vacuum at the sport's national federation and its top national team. The KFA chose to sign Moreno on a six-match contract that takes him through Nov. 27, instead of rushing to hire a full-time coach while its presidency remained vacant. results.title: Trump says he may meet with Kim Jong-un while in China
results.content: WASHINGTON — In a surprise announcement, U.S. President Donald Trump said Monday he may meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un during his upcoming trip to China. "We may meet with Kim Jong-un also, so that'll be good," Trump told reporters from the White House before leaving for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China. Trump added Chinese President Xi Jinping might invite Kim to Shenzhen when the leaders gather. Trump is scheduled to meet with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday on the sidelines of the APEC meeting. The planned trilateral meeting comes as Trump seeks a diplomatic solution to the war in Ukraine, while Washington and Beijing continue to navigate differences over trade, tariffs and other geopolitical issues. results.title: 'The Remarried Empress' paradox: Viral success also met with mockery, criticisms
results.content: “I challenge you to a duel for insulting the honor of my woman.” A line straight out of a fantasy novel is delivered by an actor and brought to life on screen. In another scene, a prince from a neighboring kingdom transforms into a bird, nestles in the empress’ arms and then turns back into a human. Far removed from anything resembling reality, the series invites viewers into an entirely new fictional universe. This is the world of Disney+ original series “The Remarried Empress.” The series has emerged as a hit, generating considerable buzz. Released on Nov. 3, it became the most-watched Disney+ local original production worldwide based on viewing figures for its first three days, setting a record among the platform’s local original titles. results.title: No grand gestures: How two Korean celebrity couples keep love alive in the spotlight
results.content: For Korean celebrities, going public with a relationship can be a risky move. Every interaction can fuel breakup rumors, while too much public affection can overshadow their careers. But two longtime celebrity couples — actors Lee Kwang-soo and Lee Sun-bin, and Red Velvet's Joy and singer Crush — are showing that romance does not have to become a public spectacle. Recent glimpses of their relationships have attracted attention for their simplicity: Lee Kwang-soo and Lee Sun-bin walking hand in hand through a shopping mall, and Joy and Crush singing together in a casual video.
